statement: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was Disney's first full-length animated movie.
why: It came out in 1937. Critics called it "Disney's Folly" before it became a massive hit.

statement: Walt Disney himself was the original voice of Mickey Mouse.
why: Walt voiced Mickey from 1928 until 1947.

statement: Steamboat Willie was the first Mickey cartoon with synchronized sound.
why: Mickey had already starred in two silent shorts, but Steamboat Willie's sound in 1928 made him a star.

statement: Walt Disney almost named Mickey Mouse "Mortimer".
why: His wife Lillian thought Mortimer sounded too stuffy and suggested Mickey instead.

statement: Mickey and Minnie Mouse share the same official birthday.
why: Both debuted in Steamboat Willie on 18 November 1928, so Disney celebrates them on the same day.

statement: Donald Duck's middle name is Fauntleroy.
why: His full name, Donald Fauntleroy Duck, appears on his draft card in the 1942 short Donald Gets Drafted.

statement: Goofy and Pluto are both dogs.
why: One walks and talks, the other doesn't, but Disney confirms they're both dogs.

statement: Toy Story was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation.
why: Pixar's Toy Story came out in 1995 as the first fully computer-animated feature.

statement: Walt Disney died before Walt Disney World opened.
why: Walt died in December 1966. The Florida resort opened in October 1971.

statement: Cinderella Castle in Florida is taller than Sleeping Beauty Castle in California.
why: Cinderella Castle is about 189 feet tall. Sleeping Beauty Castle is only about 77 feet.

statement: Disneyland in California opened in 1955.
why: It opened on 17 July 1955 in Anaheim.

statement: Elsa was the villain in early drafts of Frozen.
why: The writers changed her into a hero after hearing the song Let It Go.

statement: We Don't Talk About Bruno reached a higher chart spot than Let It Go.
why: Bruno hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2022. Let It Go peaked at No. 5.

statement: Ariel has six older sisters.
why: Aquata, Andrina, Arista, Attina, Adella and Alana. Ariel is the youngest.

statement: Flounder from The Little Mermaid isn't actually a flounder.
why: Despite his name, Disney says he's a tropical fish.

statement: Rapunzel's weapon of choice in Tangled is a frying pan.
why: She knocks out Flynn Rider with it, and it keeps coming in handy.

statement: Rapunzel's chameleon sidekick is named Pascal.
why: Pascal is her best friend in the tower.

statement: Stitch's original name is Experiment 626.
why: Dr. Jumba Jookiba created him as Experiment 626 before Lilo named him Stitch.

statement: Dopey is the only one of the Seven Dwarfs who never speaks.
why: As Happy explains, Dopey doesn't know if he can talk because he's never tried.

statement: Scar's three hyena sidekicks are Shenzi, Banzai and Ed.
why: Shenzi is the leader, Banzai is the hothead, and Ed only laughs.

statement: Ursula the sea witch is part octopus.
why: Her lower half has octopus tentacles. Six of them on screen, to be exact.

statement: Tiana from The Princess and the Frog dreams of opening her own restaurant.
why: It was a dream she shared with her late father, and it comes true at the end.

statement: Moana's pet pig is named Pua.
why: Pua is the pig. Heihei is the chicken who ends up on the boat.

statement: Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson voices Maui in Moana.
why: He also sings Maui's song, You're Welcome.

statement: Robin Williams voiced the Genie in the original Aladdin.
why: He improvised so much in 1992 that hours of extra recordings were left over.

statement: Dory from Finding Nemo has short-term memory loss.
why: She says so herself, and her sequel Finding Dory is built around it.

statement: In Encanto, Mirabel is the only Madrigal grandchild without a magical gift.
why: Her sisters and cousins all get gifts. Even little Antonio gets his early in the film.

statement: Dumbo's "magic" feather wasn't actually magic.
why: The crows gave it to him to build his confidence. He could fly with his ears all along.

statement: Lumière in Beauty and the Beast is a candelabra.
why: He's the castle's charming candelabra who leads the song Be Our Guest.

statement: Pixar's Coco is set during Día de los Muertos.
why: Miguel crosses into the Land of the Dead during Mexico's Day of the Dead holiday.

statement: Walt Disney's body was cryogenically frozen.
why: A famous myth. Walt was cremated in 1966 and his ashes rest at Forest Lawn in Glendale, California.

statement: Mickey Mouse was the first cartoon star Walt Disney created.
why: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit came first in 1927. Walt lost the rights to Universal, then created Mickey.

statement: Walt Disney animated Steamboat Willie all by himself.
why: His partner Ub Iwerks did most of the animation and helped design Mickey.

statement: One of the Seven Dwarfs is named Sniffy.
why: It's Sneezy. The seven are Doc, Grumpy, Happy, Sleepy, Bashful, Sneezy and Dopey.

statement: In The Lion King, Scar is Simba's grandfather.
why: Scar is Simba's uncle, Mufasa's younger brother.

statement: Woody's horse in Toy Story is named Buttercup.
why: Woody's horse is Bullseye. Buttercup is the unicorn from Toy Story 3.

statement: Buzz Lightyear's catchphrase is "To the stars and beyond!"
why: It's "To infinity and beyond!"

statement: Nemo's dad in Finding Nemo is named Gill.
why: His dad is Marlin. Gill is the leader of the fish tank gang.

statement: Gaston gives Belle her huge library in Beauty and the Beast.
why: The Beast gives her the library. Gaston thinks reading is a waste of time.

statement: Princess Jasmine's pet tiger is named Abu.
why: Her tiger is Rajah. Abu is Aladdin's monkey.

statement: Pinocchio's nose grows when he gets scared.
why: It grows when he tells a lie.

statement: Peter Pan's fairy friend is named Silvermist.
why: It's Tinker Bell. Silvermist is one of her fairy friends from the later Disney Fairies films.

statement: Lightning McQueen's racing number is 99.
why: Lightning McQueen is number 95.

statement: Kristoff's reindeer in Frozen is named Rudolph.
why: His reindeer is Sven.

statement: Will Smith voiced Mushu in the original Mulan.
why: Eddie Murphy voiced Mushu in 1998.

statement: "Hakuna Matata" means "live forever".
why: It's Swahili for "no worries".

statement: The original Disneyland is in Florida.
why: Disneyland is in Anaheim, California. Florida has Walt Disney World.

statement: Tinker Bell has spoken lines in the original 1953 Peter Pan.
why: She never speaks in the film. She talks through bell sounds and expressions.

statement: Cinderella's fairy godmother turns a watermelon into her carriage.
why: It's a pumpkin.

statement: Elsa builds her ice palace while singing "Into the Unknown".
why: She builds it during Let It Go. Into the Unknown is from Frozen II.

statement: The Lion King is based on Romeo and Juliet.
why: It's loosely inspired by Shakespeare's Hamlet: a murdered king, a scheming uncle and a prince who must return.

statement: Snow White falls asleep after eating a poisoned pear.
why: It's a poisoned apple.

statement: In Monsters, Inc., the city runs on children's laughter from the very start.
why: It runs on screams at first. The switch to laughter only happens at the end.

statement: Baymax comes from the movie Wreck-It Ralph.
why: Baymax is from Big Hero 6.

statement: In Up, Carl's late wife is named Edith.
why: Her name is Ellie.

statement: Phil, Hercules' trainer, is a centaur.
why: Phil is a satyr: half man, half goat.

statement: Cinderella was the first Disney princess.
why: Snow White came first in 1937. Cinderella followed in 1950.

statement: Ratatouille is set in London.
why: Remy cooks in Paris.

statement: King Triton rules the underwater kingdom of Atlantis.
why: His kingdom is Atlantica. Atlantis is a different Disney movie.

statement: Lilo & Stitch is set in California.
why: It's set on the Hawaiian island of Kauaʻi.

statement: Walt Disney's middle name was Edward.
why: His middle name was Elias, after his father.

statement: The Disney company was founded by two brothers.
why: Walt and Roy Disney started the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio in 1923.

statement: Roy Disney insisted the Florida resort be called Walt Disney World.
why: After Walt died, Roy put off retiring to finish the project and named it in his brother's honour.

statement: Walt Disney won only one Academy Award.
why: He won 22 competitive Oscars, more than anyone in history, plus four honorary ones.

statement: Minnie Mouse's full first name is Minerva.
why: Minnie is short for Minerva.

statement: Donald Duck has had a new voice actor every decade since 1934.
why: Clarence Nash voiced Donald for over 50 years, from 1934 until his death in 1985.

statement: Huey, Dewey and Louie are Donald Duck's nephews.
why: The triplets first appeared in 1937 and are often left in Donald's care.

statement: Scrooge McDuck is Donald Duck's father.
why: Scrooge is Donald's uncle.

statement: Daisy Duck is Donald Duck's girlfriend.
why: She first appeared as his sweetheart in 1940's Mr. Duck Steps Out.

statement: Jiminy Cricket acts as Pinocchio's conscience.
why: The Blue Fairy gives him the job of guiding Pinocchio.

statement: When You Wish Upon a Star comes from Cinderella.
why: It's from Pinocchio, and it won the Oscar for Best Original Song.

statement: The sorcerer in Fantasia is named Yen Sid.
why: Yen Sid is Disney spelled backwards.

statement: Dumbo's mother is named Mrs. Trunk.
why: She's called Mrs. Jumbo.

statement: Bambi's skunk friend is named Thumper.
why: Thumper is the rabbit. The skunk is called Flower.

statement: Cinderella's mouse friends are named Jaq and Gus.
why: They're always dodging Lucifer, the stepmother's cat.

statement: The Fairy Godmother's magic words are Abracadabra.
why: Her magic words are Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo.

statement: Princess Aurora is raised under the name Briar Rose.
why: The fairies hide her in the forest under that name to protect her from Maleficent.

statement: The three good fairies in Sleeping Beauty are Flora, Fauna and Tinker Bell.
why: The third is Merryweather. Tinker Bell is from Peter Pan.

statement: Maleficent turns into a dragon in Sleeping Beauty.
why: She transforms to fight Prince Phillip in the film's climax.

statement: Captain Hook lost his hand to a shark.
why: A crocodile ate it, and the croc has followed him ever since.

statement: Pongo and Perdita are the parents in 101 Dalmatians.
why: Cruella de Vil steals their puppies to make a fur coat.

statement: Lady and the Tramp share a bowl of soup in their most famous scene.
why: It's a plate of spaghetti, and their shared noodle ends in a kiss.

statement: The Jungle Book was the last animated film Walt Disney worked on.
why: Walt died in 1966, before the film came out in 1967.

statement: Baloo in The Jungle Book is a tiger.
why: Baloo is a bear. The tiger is the villain, Shere Khan.

statement: Robin Hood is a fox in Disney's 1973 film.
why: Every character is an animal, and Little John is a bear.

statement: Christopher Robin was a completely made-up character.
why: A. A. Milne named him after his real son, whose toys inspired Pooh and friends.

statement: Mary Poppins was played by Audrey Hepburn in the 1964 film.
why: Julie Andrews played her and won the Oscar for Best Actress.

statement: Disney bought Pixar in 2006.
why: The deal was worth about $7.4 billion.

statement: Disney bought Marvel in 1999.
why: Disney bought Marvel in 2009 for about $4 billion.

statement: Disney owns Star Wars.
why: Disney bought Lucasfilm from George Lucas in 2012.

statement: Disney has never owned any part of 21st Century Fox.
why: Disney bought most of 21st Century Fox in 2019, including The Simpsons and Avatar.

statement: Beauty and the Beast was the first animated film nominated for Best Picture.
why: It earned the nomination at the 1992 Oscars.

statement: Frozen was nominated for Best Picture.
why: Only three animated films have been: Beauty and the Beast, Up and Toy Story 3.

statement: Belle's father is named Maurice.
why: He's an inventor who gets lost and ends up in the Beast's castle.

statement: Chip is Mrs. Potts' son.
why: She's a teapot and he's a teacup with a chip in it.

statement: Jafar's sidekick Iago is a crow.
why: Iago is a parrot, voiced by Gilbert Gottfried.

statement: Timon is a warthog and Pumbaa is a meerkat.
why: It's the reverse: Timon is the meerkat and Pumbaa is the warthog.

statement: James Earl Jones voiced Mufasa in both the 1994 Lion King and the 2019 remake.
why: He played the role in 1994 and again in the 2019 remake.

statement: Sebastian in The Little Mermaid is a lobster.
why: Sebastian is a crab, and he's King Triton's court composer.

statement: Ariel calls a fork a dinglehopper.
why: Scuttle tells her it's for combing hair, and she believes him.

statement: The Little Mermaid and Frozen are both based on Hans Christian Andersen stories.
why: Frozen is loosely based on his tale The Snow Queen.

statement: Mulan joins the army to take her brother's place.
why: She takes her elderly father's place. Mulan has no brother in the film.

statement: Pocahontas was a fictional character invented by Disney.
why: She was a real Powhatan woman from Virginia, though the film changes much of her story.

statement: Pocahontas has a pet fox named Meeko.
why: Meeko is a raccoon.

statement: Quasimodo's gargoyle friends are named Victor, Hugo and Laverne.
why: Victor and Hugo are a nod to Victor Hugo, who wrote the original novel.

statement: Hercules' winged horse is named Phil.
why: The horse is Pegasus. Phil is the satyr who trains Hercules.

statement: Phil Collins won an Oscar for a song from Tarzan.
why: You'll Be in My Heart won Best Original Song.

statement: In Lilo & Stitch, 'ohana' means family.
why: Lilo teaches Stitch that in an ohana nobody gets left behind.

statement: Tiana was Disney's first African-American princess.
why: The Princess and the Frog came out in 2009 and is set in New Orleans.

statement: Flynn Rider's real name is Hans.
why: His real name is Eugene Fitzherbert. Hans is the villain in Frozen.

statement: Frozen takes place in the kingdom of Arendelle.
why: The fictional kingdom is inspired by Norway.

statement: Frozen won two Academy Awards.
why: It won Best Animated Feature, and Let It Go won Best Original Song.

statement: Merida from Brave is from Ireland.
why: Brave is set in Scotland. Merida was also Pixar's first princess.

statement: Heihei the chicken in Moana is voiced by Alan Tudyk.
why: Tudyk has voiced characters in many Disney animated films.

statement: In Zootopia, Judy Hopps is a fox and Nick Wilde is a rabbit.
why: Judy is the rabbit police officer and Nick is the fox.

statement: Big Hero 6 is set in a city called San Fransokyo.
why: The city is a mash-up of San Francisco and Tokyo.

statement: Vanellope von Schweetz comes from the game Hero's Duty.
why: She's a racer from Sugar Rush. Hero's Duty is a shooter game in Wreck-It Ralph.

statement: Tom Hanks voices Woody and Tim Allen voices Buzz Lightyear.
why: They've played the roles since the first Toy Story in 1995.

statement: The lamp in Pixar's logo is named Pixie.
why: It's named Luxo Jr., after Pixar's 1986 short film.

statement: The code A113 is hidden in many Pixar films.
why: It's the number of a classroom at CalArts, where many Pixar animators studied.

statement: The Pizza Planet truck only appears in the Toy Story films.
why: It's hidden in almost every Pixar film, and fans love spotting it.

statement: Monsters University is a sequel set after Monsters, Inc.
why: It's a prequel showing how Mike and Sulley met in college.

statement: In Up, Carl's house is lifted by balloons.
why: Carl ties thousands of balloons to it to fly to South America.

statement: WALL-E is named after a Pixar animator called Walter Lee.
why: WALL-E is an acronym for Waste Allocation Load Lifter: Earth-Class.

statement: In Ratatouille, Remy controls Linguini by pulling his hair.
why: Hiding under Linguini's hat, Remy steers him around the kitchen.

statement: Edna Mode in The Incredibles is voiced by Meryl Streep.
why: She's voiced by Brad Bird, the film's director.

statement: Lightning McQueen is named after actor Steve McQueen.
why: He's named after Pixar animator Glenn McQueen, who died in 2002.

statement: The five emotions in Inside Out are Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear and Disgust.
why: They live in the mind of an 11-year-old girl named Riley.

statement: Crush the sea turtle is voiced by Finding Nemo's director.
why: Andrew Stanton directed the film and voiced the laid-back turtle.

statement: Tokyo Disneyland was the first Disney park outside the United States.
why: It opened in 1983.

statement: Disneyland Paris opened in 1982.
why: It opened in 1992, under the name Euro Disney.

statement: Hong Kong Disneyland opened in 2005.
why: It was Disney's second resort in Asia, after Tokyo.

statement: Shanghai Disneyland was Disney's first park in Asia.
why: Tokyo came first in 1983. Shanghai opened in 2016.

statement: Epcot's name is an acronym.
why: It stands for Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow, a city Walt once dreamed of building.

statement: Epcot's giant silver sphere is called the Globe of Tomorrow.
why: It's called Spaceship Earth.

statement: It's a Small World was first built for the 1964 New York World's Fair.
why: It was moved to Disneyland after the fair ended.

statement: The Haunted Mansion is home to 13 ghosts.
why: It's home to 999 happy haunts, with room for one more.

statement: Disney hides Mickey Mouse shapes all over its parks.
why: Fans call them Hidden Mickeys and hunt for them on rides, walls and even floors.

statement: Disneyland has a secret members-only club called Club 33.
why: It's tucked away in New Orleans Square and has a very long waiting list.

statement: Magic Kingdom has tunnels beneath it for staff.
why: Called utilidors, they let cast members move around without being seen.

statement: The windows on Main Street U.S.A. advertise real shops.
why: The names on them honour people who helped build Disney.

statement: The Mickey Mouse Club first aired in 1975.
why: It debuted in 1955, the same year Disneyland opened.

statement: Disney Channel launched in 2003.
why: It launched in 1983 as a paid premium channel.

statement: Disney+ first launched in 2015.
why: It first launched in November 2019.

statement: Magic Kingdom is the most visited theme park in the world.
why: It regularly tops the yearly attendance rankings, with around 17 million visitors.
